text:
The Overmountain Men Invoke the Sword of the Lord and Gideon —

Major Patrick Ferguson’s threat against the western settlements helped inspire a military response among the frontier Patriots. Isaac Shelby, an experienced frontiersman and soldier, received Ferguson’s message from Samuel Phillips after Shelby and his men had returned across the mountains following the American defeat at Camden. 

Shelby rode about 40 miles to meet John Sevier, Commander of the Washington County militia. After discussing the danger facing their isolated settlements, Shelby and Sevier decided that an immediate offensive offered their best defense.

Shelby and Sevier needed additional troops before they could challenge Ferguson. They contacted Colonel William Campbell of Virginia and Colonel Charles McDowell of North Carolina. Campbell initially preferred to defend the frontier and allow Ferguson to move farther from General Charles Cornwallis. Shelby urged him to reconsider, arguing that the expedition needed Campbell’s men. Campbell agreed, as did McDowell, and the leaders called for a general gathering at Sycamore Shoals on the Watauga River on September 25.

The expedition also required money and supplies. John Adair allowed Sevier to use public funds belonging to North Carolina, while Sevier and Shelby personally promised repayment of the approximately $12,000 or $13,000 used for ammunition and supplies. Frontier communities ground corn into meal, produced gunpowder, mined lead, gathered livestock and horses, and prepared clothing for the soldiers.

More than 1,000 settlers gathered at Sycamore Shoals. Sevier brought 240 men, Shelby approximately 240, Campbell 400 and McDowell 160. Other militia forces planned to join them during the march. The army traveled without uniforms or an organized supply train, and many men carried long rifles, blankets and simple provisions.

On September 26, Clergyman Samuel Doak prayed for the expedition and gave the soldiers the battle cry, “The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!” The men then mounted their horses and rode across the mountains in search of Ferguson.

1. Gathering of the Overmountain Men at Sycamore Shoals by Lloyd Branson. Source: Tennessee State Museum Website.

FLORIDA MAN OFFERS COPS A VODKA SPRITZER DURING 100 MPH CHASE

FORT MYERS, FLORIDA — Dennis Kravitz, 52, was arrested Friday night after allegedly leading deputies on a high-speed chase reaching over 100 miles per hour, then slowing just enough to hand a freshly mixed vodka spritzer out the window to the pursuing patrol car.

Deputies say the offer came as a genuine surprise mid-pursuit.

Deputies reported Kravitz had a small cooler and mixing setup visible on the passenger seat throughout the chase
Witnesses say he slowed to nearly a stop at one point specifically to extend the drink toward the patrol car window
He allegedly shouted "no hard feelings, it's a good batch" before speeding off again
Deputies say the spritzer itself was garnished with a lime wedge, prepared with clear care despite the circumstances
Witnesses reported he attempted the same offer a second time roughly two miles later, with a fresh drink
He reportedly told officers after his eventual arrest that he "just wanted the chase to feel civil"

The chase ended when Kravitz's vehicle ran low on fuel roughly fifteen miles from where it began.

"In nineteen years in law enforcement, I've been through plenty of pursuits, but never one that included a hospitality offer," said Deputy Sheriff Glen Ashworth, a 19-year veteran of the Lee County Sheriff's Office.

Both spritzers were logged into evidence, still cold. Neither was accepted.

He offered drinks mid-chase. Deputies offered handcuffs instead.
Some gestures simply don't land at a hundred miles an hour.

text:
In memory of Lorraine D. Antigua
September 27, 1968 – September 11, 2001

Age 32 Middletown, New Jersey, Cantor Fitzgerald, Securities Lending North Tower, 104th floor

Lorraine was a mother, a fiancée, a colleague people liked to sit near, and a woman who had already built a life she was proud of. She had two children, Aaron and Caitlin. She was engaged to Brian Wilkes. 

They had bought a house together in Middletown and were planning a family under one roof. They planted azaleas and sunflowers in the garden. They talked about getting married on a Harley, maybe at a drive-through chapel in Las Vegas. She said she would buy the bike.

She loved her work. Friends said she turned down other offers because she liked the securities lending desk at Cantor Fitzgerald. She had started young, working at the World Trade Center as a teenager in a co-op program at First Boston and she stayed in that world. 

People remembered her smile first. She came in bright. She was generous, an avid reader, a scuba diver. She made fried rice for the kids the night of September 10.

On the morning of September 11 she was at her desk on the 104th floor when American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower. At 8:50 a.m. she left a message on Brian’s phone: a plane had hit her building, but she was okay. He never reached her again. No one from Cantor Fitzgerald who was in the firm’s offices that morning survived.

Those who knew her still speak of her in the present tense. “She’s awesome,” Brian said. “She ruined me for other women.” Friends recalled lunches, margaritas with no salt, a striped sweater and a fisherman’s hat at a barbecue two days before. Her mother remembered a daughter who had come out of Brooklyn and built something of her own.

Lorraine D. Antigua is remembered as a woman who loved her children, her work, her garden, and the life she was still making. 

Lorraine is not forgotten.
Never forget.❤️🙏

text:
Happy Birthday Betsy Drake
One of the most promising and unique actresses of her generation, Drake gave up stardom to marry Cary Grant. Wouldn’t we all? Betsy was the eldest child of American expatriates, and was born in Paris. Her grandfather, Tracy Drake, had opened the Drake Hotel in Chicago on New Year's Eve, 1920, but the family lost their money in the 1929 stock-market crash. As a result, Betsy returned to the U.S. with her parents, brothers, and a nanny. She grew up in Chicago, Connecticut, Washington, DC, Virginia and New York City, attending 12 different schools, before taking acting lessons at The National Park Seminary. She began looking for work in New York, supporting herself by modelling, and soon met the playwright Horton Foote, who offered her a job as an understudy in “Only the Heart”. After coming to the attention of producer Hal Wallis, Drake was pressured by her agent into signing a Hollywood contract. She loathed the film community and managed to engineer her release by pretending to be insane. Drake returned to New York, and, in 1947, read for Elia Kazan for the lead role in the play “Deep Are the Roots”. Later that year, Drake was selected by the director as one of the founding members of the Actors Studio. Cary Grant spotted her in 1947 while she was performing for Kazan in London. The couple, who both happened to be returning to the U.S. on the Queen Mary, were instantly attracted to one another. Drake was petite, beautiful, clever and had a huskily sexy voice. At Grant’s insistence, she was signed to a film contract by RKO  and David Selznick. In her first picture, she appeared opposite Grant, in the romantic comedy “Every Girl Should Be Married” (1948). A natural on screen, she won rave reviews for her droll performance. New York Times film critic Bosley Crowther called her “a lovely actress….foxily amusing….and more than a match for Mr Grant.” The world was now her oyster, but she rejected the film offers that came in for another offer entirely. On Christmas Day, 1949, Drake and Grant married in a private ceremony organized by the star’s best man, Howard Hughes. The couple chose a low-key if eccentric domestic life. They experimented with transcendentalism, mysticism, yoga and LSD. In 1954, they bought the "Las Palomas" estate in Palm Springs, California. House guests included good friends David Niven, who adored Betsy, and Randolph Scott. The Grants co-starred in the radio series “Mr. and Mrs. Blandings”, and appeared together in the comedy drama “Room for One More” (1952). Drake took leading roles in England and the U.S. and a supporting role in the film “Will Success Spoil Rock Hunter?” (1957). All was fair weather until Grant was hit by the Italian bombshell Sophia Loren, and fell hard whilst working with her in Spain. His next film was supposed to be “Houseboat” (1958). Betsy had written the script under a pseudonym for herself and her husband. Grant arranged for Loren to take Drake's place, with a rewritten screenplay. Their affair had already ended, however, which caused bitterness and tension on the set. Grant and Drake separated in 1958, and divorced in 1962. Their marriage was the actor’s longest and happiest union and he was a fool to have become involved with Loren. Grant credited Betsy with broadening his interests beyond acting, and with introducing him to LSD therapy and hypnosis. Drake herself took LSD as a way of recovering from the trauma of the divorce. She never remarried. Betsy Drake Grant spent the latter part of her life in London, where she died, aged 92, on October 27, 2015. Her last screen appearance was in the documentary film “Cary Grant: A Class Apart” (2005), in which she reflected on their  time together, and denied rumors that he was a homosexual.

The proposal came after Maduro’s capture ended free Venezuelan oil and Mexico stopped shipments, leaving Cuba increasingly fuel-starved.

Cuba, which produces only about 40% of its energy needs, would have gained reliable fuel and investment while Washington became its main oil supplier.

The talks collapsed because Havana feared dependence on a U.S.-controlled energy company, while Rodríguez Castro was open to economic reforms but rejected U.S. demands over Cuba’s leadership. 

“The Cubans were not there yet,” a source said. The negotiations also triggered backlash from Cuban-American Republicans concerned about preserving the Castro system, while Rodríguez Castro faced criticism in Cuba after his role and lavish lifestyle became public.

That is not continuity, but the definition of treating a defined condemnation as a reformable dead letter.  By this very theology : arianism, monophysitism,  monothelitism, protestantism, jansenism and all solemny condemned heretical doctrines could now become doctrine  -  which is exactly what the Vatican II latrocinium introduced by its imposition of the synthesis of all heresies.

To boldy say 'Nobody holds Quanta Cura anymore' is not historical sophistication, it is heretical depravity dressed as pastoral realism.  DH does not 'develop' Quanta Cura - it asserts the exact proposition Pius IX condemned, then builds a civil and ecclesial system on top of it.

On 8 December 1864 Pius IX, as pastor of the universal Church, by his apostolic authority reproved, prescribed, and condemned the claim that liberty of conscience and of worship is a proper right of every man, which must be proclaimed and asserted by law in every well-constituted society.  He made this doctrinal definition :

Itaque omnes et singulas (3) pravas opiniones ac doctrinas singillatim **hisce Litteris** commemoratas (2) auctoritate Nostra Apostolica (1) reprobamus, proscribimus atque damnamus, easque (4) ab omnibus Catholicæ Ecclesiæ filiis, veluti reprobatas, proscriptas atque damnatas omnino (1) haberi volumus et mandamus.

Quanta Cura is EX CATHEDRA because Pius IX (1) made definitive and binding condamnation (2) as Pastor and Teacher of all Christians and in virtue of his supreme Apostolic authority (3) regarding faith or morals (4) to be held by all the Church. He who refuses to accept the solemn definitions of the Pope, or who even doubts them, sins against faith; and should he remain obstinate in this unbelief, he would no longer be a Catholic, but a heretic:

We teach and define as a divinely revealed dogma that
when the Roman pontiff speaks EX CATHEDRA,that is, when,
in the exercise of his office as shepherd and teacher of all Christians,
in virtue of his supreme apostolic authority,
he defines a doctrine concerning faith or morals to be held by the whole church,
he possesses,by the divine assistance promised to him in blessed Peter,
that infallibility which the divine Redeemer willed his church to enjoy in defining doctrine concerning faith or morals.
Therefore, such definitions of the Roman pontiff are of themselves, and not by the consent of the church, irreformable.
So then, should anyone, which God forbid, have the temerity to reject this definition of ours: let him be anathema.
-PASTOR AETERNUS.

Quanta Cura and the Syllabus of Errors form a single integrated document. Quanta Cura contains the general doctrine, arranged in chapters while its Syllabus contains the specific condemned propositions, arranged in canons or in elenchus form - together they are one program. The encyclical establishes the doctrine itself while the Syllabus specify the particular errors that contradict said defined doctrine. This unity of structure means the four marks of an ex cathedra pronouncement apply across both parts as a coherent teaching act.

The First Vatican Council's dogmatic constitution Dei Filius forbids giving defined doctrine another sense than the Church has given it:

N° III.  If anyone says that
it is possible that at some time, 
given the advancement of knowledge, 
a sense may be assigned to the dogmas
propounded by the church which is different
from that which the church has understood
and understands: let him be anathema.
-DEI FILIUS, CHAPTER 4. ON FAITH AND REASON

Dignitatis Humanae begins with a courtesy. It said that Religious Freedom "leaves untouched traditional Catholic doctrine on the moral duty of men and societies toward the true religion and toward the one Church of Christ" (DH 1). Keep that sentence in MIND ... It is the courtesy that makes the rest drinkable. 

Pius VI in Auctorem Fidei already condemned innovators which hide tortuous maneuvers under ambiguity, then by slight additions distort the confession necessary for salvation, and that the perverse meaning under the veil of ambiguity must be named : In order not to shock the ears of Catholics, the innovators sought to hide the subtleties of their tortuous maneuvers by the use of seemingly innocuous words such as would allow them to insinuate error into souls in the most gentle manner. Once the truth had been compromised, they could, by means of slight changes or additions in phraseology, distort the confession of the faith that is necessary for our salvation. Whenever it becomes necessary to expose statements that disguise some suspected error or danger under the veil of ambiguity, one must denounce the perverse meaning under which the error opposed to Catholic truth is camouflaged. "Leaves untouched" is the veil. What follows is the meaning.

In the same breath the Council says the one true religion "subsists" in the Catholic and Apostolic Church (DH 1; LG 8), and yet its companion texts place "elements of sanctification and of truth" outside her (LG 8; UR 3; NA 2). That is already Syll. prop. 16, 17, and 18: salvation in the observance of any religion, good hope for those not in the true Church, Protestantism as another form of the same true religion. If those outside the Church are means of sanctification, the city must be told that it may not treat the outside as a public disorder. Then DH 1 adds that the Council draws from the treasury of Tradition "new things that are in harmony with the things that are old." Harmony, here, means this: keep the nouns of the old duty, empty them of every public effect. If societies still owe honor to the one Church, they cannot be bound to title the cult of error. If they are bound to title it, the duty is a husk (Syll. prop. 55, 77, 79). The deposit does not grow a contradictory right outside the unity of defined dogma as Dei Filius forbade another sense of defined doctrine under anathema. "New things in harmony with the old," when the new thing is the civil right of error, is not growth. It is the old condemned under a new name.

Quanta Cura did not strike a place in time - it struck a system, just like Popes condemned all other heresies before. It named as a deliramentum and libertas perditionis the claim that liberty of conscience and of worship is a proper right of every man, which law must proclaim in every well-constituted society. (Syll. prop. 15) DH 2 recites the contradictory as if it were a discovery of the Gospel: the person has a right to religious freedom, rooted in dignity known from the Word of God and from reason, and this right must be recognized as a civil right. Dignity in the 'Pastoral' constitution (GS 12-22) is defined as the inviolable status of the person by reason, free will, and liberty of conscience. Quanta Cura had already named that liberty, once made a civil title, a liberty of perdition. DH 1 baptizes the modern "awareness" of it and the demand to act by one's own options (Syll. prop. 3, 4, 15). Reason as measure of the religious choice is not an ornament. It is the first principle. If reason without the rule of revealed truth is arbiter of the cult a man will publicly keep, the State has no remaining title to prefer the altar of Christ to the altar of the idol. What DH teaches in not only a doctrine contrary to defined dogma (eg definition on Papal Infallibility) - it imposes the modernist heresy as a rule of faith (cf. S. Pius X, Pascendi).

Watch how the principle locks itself. DH 2 says no one is to be forced against conscience, nor prevented from acting according to it, privately or publicly, alone or associated, within "just limits," and that this exemption persists even in those who do not fulfill the duty of seeking and adhering to the truth, provided a "just public order" remains. That last clause is the bolt on the door as Pius IX condemned the doctrine that the best condition of society is one in which public power has no duty to restrain offenders against the Catholic religion except when public peace requires it. DH 2 and DH 7 write that condemned exception as the only limit left (Syll. prop. 19, 24, 40, 55, 77, 79). The man who refuses the truth keeps the title. Error ceases to be a wound in the city. Error, heresy, apostsy and idolatry - even demon worship - becomes a God given right.

The civil right is not only the erring man. It is the erring body. Pius IX condemned the claim that it is no longer expedient that the Catholic religion be the religion of the State to the exclusion of other worship (Syll. prop. 24, 77), and the claim that strangers should by law enjoy the public exercise of their own peculiar worship in christendom (Syll. prop. 78). It condemned the further claim that civil liberty of every worship, and the full power of publishing any opinions, does not corrupt minds or spread the pest of indifferentism (Syll. prop. 79). DH 4-6 take the condemned claim and make it the charter of the sect as such. Communities, without distinction of true and false, must govern themselves by their own norms, honor the "supreme divinity" in public, teach, form ministers, hold goods, and display "the special value of their doctrine for organizing society and inspiring the whole of human activity" (DH 4). That is Syllabus (prop. 15, 16, 21, 77, 78, 79, 80) in one grant. Proposition 21 had already struck the assertion that the Church cannot define dogmatically that the Catholic religion is the only true religion - DH 1 does not need to recite that assertion. What it does no say, it puts into action. The word "subsists" can remain in DH 1. The law of DH 4 has already made it idle. The Council teaches one true religion in DH 1 as a false demonstration of integrity, yet in imposed its contrary are a rule of faith.

Once the sect is a subject of rights, the Church cannot remain what Quanta Cura defended. Pius IX (Syll. prop. 19) struck the claim that the Church is not a true and perfect society, free, with perpetual rights from her Founder, and that civil power may define those rights and their limits. The same Roman Pontiff (Syll. prop. 20) condemned the claim that ecclesiastical authority may not act without the government's assent as well as the claim that the Church has no power of using force, nor any temporal power, direct or indirect (Syll. prop. 24). DH 3 answers all three at once: the civil power exceeds its limits if it directs or impedes religious acts. The unique liberty of the Church is folded into a generic liberty that belongs equally to the conventicle (Syll. prop. 19, 21, 24). DH 13 then completes the exchange. Where the modern regime of religious liberty exists, the Church is said to find her ideal conditions (Syll. prop. 19, 55, 80). The liberty of truth and the civil liberty of error are offered as one and the same.

The State is rewritten to match. Quanta Cura condemned ruling the people as if religion were not there. 
That is Syll. prop. 55: Church separated from State, State from Church, as a principle. 
Syll. prop. 39 and 56 struck the recasting of public law as a mere catalogue of rights detached from the true cult. DH 6 makes the State's "essential duty" the protection and promotion of the inviolable rights invented in DH 2-5, including the rights of false communities. 
The common good becomes the set of conditions in which those rights are enjoyed by secular standards (Syll. prop. 39, 56, 77). 
DH 5 carries the same title into the house and the school: the family orders its religion and chooses its schools by its own conviction (Syll. prop. 15, 47, 48). City, hearth, and classroom become instruments of the same grant. 
DH 7 pretends to limit it, but the limits are circular as they must not touch the content of falsehood and they may only keep a peace that already includes the equal right of error to organize (Syll. prop. 77, 79) : "Just public order" is not the peace of Christ, but the peace of the new first principle of liberty, equality and fraternity defending itself.

Here the system becomes satanic and apostate in the proper sense. DH 3 still names the eternal law as the supreme norm. Then it lodges the perception of that law in the already solemny condemned doctrine of liberty conscience in Quanta Cura. Then it concludes that a man must not be prevented from acting according to that conscience in public (Syll. prop. 15, 79). To refuse the free public exercise of religion, once secular "public order" is safe, is called an injury to the person and to the order God Himself established (Syll. prop. 24, 77). Pius IX had condemned a proposition as an error that must not be held. DH 3 makes the contradictory a command of God upon Caesar. It is not giving unto Cesar what is Cesar's, but robbing God from what is trully God's. On that showing, the public law of Christian ages, and Leo X in Exsurge Domine, prop. 33 (condemning the claim that "to burn heretics is against the will of the Spirit"), would be injuries to the divine order. Prop. 33 does not turn the scaffold into a sacrament - it refuses the Lutheran claim that the Church's public defense of the faith is against the Holy Ghost. 

DH 3 takes the condemned side: the magistrate "exceeds his limits" if he impedes religious acts. The prince is no longer the minister of God for the true cult. He is the warden of every cult and the Devil (Syll. prop. 19, 55, 56). Auctorem Fidei and Exsurge Domine are not distant ornaments here for they are are the earlier names of the same war: evangelical diction thrown over the disarming of the Church, solemny condemned by the extraordinary pontifical magisterium. DH 3 teaches that disarming is obedience to God - thus every military action the Church perpetrated, the Holy Roman Inquisition and all the Roman Pontiffs who protected christendom are declare by DH to have sinned and err'd in their faith and morals. The system therefore writes itself a past. DH 9-12 say the doctrine is founded in Revelation, that Christ and the Apostles handed it on, that the Church has kept and transmitted it, and that former practices contrary to it failed the Gospel (Syll. prop. 5, 80). If fifteen centuries of public law were a failure to understand the Apostles, then it is implicit that the Church has imposed error since its very first ecumenical Council according to this heretical document.

This is why Pius IX had already condemned the claim that the Roman Pontiff can and ought to reconcile himself with progress, liberalism, and modern civilization. (Syll. prop. 80) DH 15 salutes international charters and modern constitutions as favorable signs and calls a juridical guarantee of religious liberty necessary for the peace of peoples (Syll. prop. 77, 79, 80). The world that hissed at the Syllabus is invited to countersign the Council. Dignity founds the right. The right founds the new common good. The new common good founds the new history. From Karl Streed -

I BET YOU DIDN'Y KNOW ABOUT THIS: AFTER FLIGHT 77 HIT THE PENTAGON ON 9/11, THE FOLLOWING HAPPENED.

A daycare facility inside the Pentagon had many children, including infants who were in heavy cribs. The daycare supervisor, looking at all the children they needed to evacuate, was in a panic over what they could do.

There were many children, mostly toddlers, as well as the infants who would need to be taken out with the cribs. There was no time to try to bundle them into carriers and strollers.

Just then a young Marine came running into the center and asked what they needed. After hearing what the center director was trying to do, he ran back out into the hallway and disappeared. The director thought, "Well, here we are, on our own."

About 2 minutes later, that Marine returned with 40 other Marines in tow.

Each of them grabbed a crib with a child, and the rest started gathering up toddlers.

The director and her staff then helped them take all the children out of the center and down toward the park near the Potomac .

Once they got about 3/4 of a mile outside the building, the Marines stopped in the park, and then did a fabulous thing - they formed a circle with the cribs, which were quite sturdy and heavy, like the covered wagons in the Old West.

Inside this circle of cribs, they put the toddlers, to keep them from wandering off. 

Outside this circle were the 40 Marines, forming a perimeter around the children and waiting for instructions. There they remained until the parents could be notified and come get their children.

The chaplain then said, "I don't think any of us saw nor heard of this on any of the news stories of the day. It was an incredible story of our men there.” There wasn't a dry eye in the room.

The thought of those Marines and what they did and how fast they reacted; could we expect any less from them? It was one of the most touching stories from the Pentagon.

It's the military, not the politicians that ensures our right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. 

It's the military who salutes the flag, who serves beneath the flag, and whose coffin is draped by the flag.

If you care to offer the smallest token of recognition and appreciation for the military, please pass this on and pray for our men and women, who have served and are currently serving our country, and honor the memory of those who have given the ultimate sacrifice!

God Bless The USA!

🚨 State of Laser Adress 🚨

It has been a rough week boys and girls, not gonna lie.

The deal for the workshop fell through. I am feeling all sorts of ways about it, but at this point there is really nothing I can do about it. The seller originally had the building listed for $140,000. Not a single person interested in it, and by the time we looked at it, the asking price was $110,000. After looking at the building, and see that it was very neglected over the last 50 years, we made an offer for $80,000. They countered with $100,000 and we agreed, because it would be affordable for us, and we had a vision of how we could take care of the neglect and make it our own. 

The bank approved everything, and as many of you know, if you are getting a loan for property, you need an appraisal. The bank and the appraiser took their time (it is S Louisiana and things move slow) but the appraisal finally came back, and it came in at $56,000. Much lower than I or the seller was expecting, but the appraisal was thorough and very detailed, and I agreed with it. With all the work that needed to get done, the appraisal was right. 

So, we sent our counter offer to the seller, and they did not agree. They wanted $80,000, and the bank will not loan anything over the appraised price. There would have been an option for us to pay the difference in cash, but that would have completely emptied our accounts from the money we were going to use to fix the place up. The seller was not willing to budge on the price (I know what I got sonny!) even though a professional appraiser was telling them otherwise. So, unfortunately we had to walk away. The whole ending put a very sour taste in my mouth about the building and seller, so I truly feel like I am dodging a bullet, but that is neither here nor there. 

This area doesn't have many options available when it comes to these types of workshops, so we are back on the search again. I am absolutely determined to be in a new workshop by the end of the year, even if it means buying a whole ass house and turning it into the House of Laser! 

NGL, the whole thing made me feel a bit depressed. I put every ounce of energy into making this place a reality, and it drained me. I pushed myself harder and further than I ever have, and the deal not working out sent my head spinning. 

So, in the meantime, we will be doing our normal thing, still putting out crispy lasered patches, mags and mugs, but the only downfall is that the FFL will have to wait. It WILL happen, just not at this very moment. 

It has been a long exhausting ride, and it will be again, but I want to say thank you to our whole community that we have built here. Literally none of this would have been possible without y'all. I appreciate each and every one of y'all more than you know.

TL;DR -- your anxieties are understandable, and AI does bring some very real risks. That said, there are three very compelling reasons to believe that any extreme existential threat presented by AI is no different from the normal existential threats that humans ignore as incredibly unlikely.  Well, there's no conspiracy or narrative likely going on. Many of the tech individuals who are telling these stories are likely falling victim to echo chambers.

_____ 

Start by realizing that this entire narrative is designed specifically to manipulate you into having the feelings that you're having right now. People have predicted doomsday from a variety of new technological, biological, religious, and atmospheric phenomena throughout human history. 

To be clear, it's not stupidity. The people who develop these models are incredibly smart. They're very conscientious, and they genuinely do believe what they're saying. 

Instead, what we're seeing here is an emergent cultural phenomenon that is unique to Bay Area tech/Silicon Valley culture. There are several reasons to have a fair degree of confidence that this is more an emergent cultural phenomenon than a genuine belief based on statistics and outcomes that are actually likely to happen:

1. Consistent slogans and language: the format of posts regarding the danger of AI, recursive self-improvement, and artificial superintelligence is very consistent. It features a widely ranging percentage to represent the likelihood of human extinction and uses a variety of emotionally charged adjectives that tell you nothing about how the result came about and only tell you about how bad the end result is. Most of the posts pretty much leave it there and, for credibility, rely on their expert credentials, declining to offer a single concretized detail as to how this extinction-level event might or might not come about. Those posts that do offer some sort of vignette skip right to the moment before Armageddon is unleashed, painting some presumed Mary Sue picture of an AI that has somehow already gained access to some bio weapon, some lab, or some collection of chemicals. Not a single post I've seen ever makes any reference to the story, the mechanisms, or how we get from where we are today to systems of such weakness, vulnerability, and apparent lack of foresight. The engineers designing this critical infrastructure apparently just waved their hands in the air and said, "It'll be fine." 

2. That leads right into point number two: the consistent failure to describe any intermediate steps that condition the critical infrastructure that AI is supposedly so likely to be able to invade strongly suggests that those who espouse the opinion adopted it from others rather than arriving at it through a reasoned approach to first principles. A structured exercise of thinking about AI risk based on first principles without a preexisting narrative would necessarily encompass the comparatively basic task of considering what actions and interventions can and should be implemented right now to try to head off some of these risks. After all, there's no difference between identifying the vulnerability and identifying the item to be redressed. All of this suggests that these folks, incredibly high IQ and hardworking as they may be, are falling victim to echo chambers and groupthink. Moreover, many of them have an incredible virtue-signaling incentive to present themselves as effective altruists: the people who are "so earnestly trying to do the right thing when they could be off making money and being evil." But instead, they're really working hard, even though there are so many ethical dilemmas! And so, even though they're making millions and millions of dollars every single year, really, they're working for the good of humanity. 

3. Another important thing to consider (that isn't a primary motivator but must be articulated): OpenAI, and Anthropic have a lot to gain from increased regulation in the AI space. Right now, their gross profit margins on the AI services they sell to enterprises and individuals are fairly healthy, but competitors from China and elsewhere are catching up fast. We're starting to get to the point where there are fewer and fewer distinctions between the capabilities of the top models. If the product you're selling isn't distinguishable from the next guy's, then you're in a situation where your product has become a commodity. Whenever things get commoditized, the price decreases dramatically. OpenAI and Anthropic cannot survive as businesses if their profit margins on model services are in the low single digits, as is the case with most commodity markets. Something that can turn this fortune around is shrinking the number of players in the market by designating OpenAI and Anthropic as trusted partners and not allowing anybody else to play in the space of frontier model development. That is "regulatory capture."
